subject: Post-incident log hold: preservation scope and privacy constraints
messages:
From: Jared Cole <security@acme-corp.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-11-22T08:12:00-05:00
Subject: RE: Possible customer-impacting incident — request to preserve logs

Hi Soojin,

We opened an incident this morning (Acme internal IRT) related to unusual API retry patterns from our app between 2026-11-21 22:30 UTC and 2026-11-22 01:10 UTC. Our legal team has requested we place a preservation hold on any Redwood logs (request/response traces, access logs, and any associated request metadata) that could contain session identifiers, IP addresses, or other PII while we investigate.

Specific asks:
- Confirm whether Redwood will preserve raw logs for the timeframe noted and prevent any automatic deletion or lifecycle processing.
- Confirm the AWS region(s) where those logs are stored and whether a copy can be made to a customer-provided, encrypted bucket for independent forensics.
- Provide a simple chain-of-custody note or manifest that indicates who captured the snapshot and where it is stored.
- Advise whether logs contain customer PII; if so, indicate options for redacted exports.

I attached a short zip with screenshots from our monitoring that show the relevant timestamps. Legal has also sent a PDF asking for a formal hold acknowledgement (attached to this thread). Please let me know if you need a signed form or POA.

Thanks — time is sensitive, so a quick acknowledgement that you received this and will hold data would be appreciated.

— Jared
Security Operations
Acme Corp
Attachment: incident-screenshots.zip
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Jared Cole <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, legal@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-11-22T09:01:00-05:00
Subject: Re: RE: Possible customer-impacting incident — request to preserve logs

Jared — thanks for flagging this and for the screenshots. I acknowledge receipt and we will place an immediate hold on lifecycle deletion for any buckets/indices that may contain logs for the timeframe you mentioned.

Couple quick clarifying questions so our preserve/export aligns with your needs:
- Can you confirm which Acme app/service this concerns (service name or customer id) so we can scope the snapshot?
- Do you need the full raw traces (including headers and bodies) or only metadata + request/response hashes?
- Is Acme requesting a cross-region copy to EU for your internal team, or is a US-region encrypted export sufficient?

I've looped in Marcus (Operations) and Karthik (Security) to coordinate the technical snapshot and chain-of-custody. We can provision an immutable snapshot and produce a manifest, then provide either: (a) a Redwood-managed encrypted export to an Acme S3 bucket (you must provide bucket ARN and KMS key), or (b) a staged download of a redacted subset.

We can start the preservation steps immediately and will confirm timeline once Marcus replies with the retention/export plan. If legal needs a signed acknowledgement, please forward the hold form — we will have our legal team sign and return.

— Soojin Lee
Head of Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, Jared Cole <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, legal@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-11-22T11:35:00-05:00
Subject: Re: RE: Possible customer-impacting incident — request to preserve logs

Quick operational plan from my side — will proceed after Soojin confirms scope:
1) Identification: query our request index for Acme customer id / service name and the time window 2026-11-21T22:30:00Z — 2026-11-22T01:10:00Z.
2) Snapshot: create an immutable forensic snapshot (read-only copy) of matching objects and store in us-east-1 forensic bucket with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS). Snapshot will include access manifest with object UUIDs and SHA256 hashes.
3) Chain-of-custody: generate a manifest that contains: snapshot id, creator (Marcus Lin), timestamp, S3 path, KMS key id, and the list of internal accounts that accessed the snapshot during capture. We will sign the manifest with an internal audit key and provide the signed manifest to Acme.
4) Export options:
   - Export A: Redwood-managed push to acme-provided S3 ARN (requires bucket policy and KMS key ID).
   - Export B: Redacted export (IP/session id masked) prepared by Redwood and delivered as encrypted archive.
5) Retention: we can set the forensic snapshot retention to 365 days (immutable) and disable lifecycle deletion for the source indices/buckets for at least 90 days or until Acme notifies us to release.

Notes: our logs may include IP addresses and session identifiers; in some cases request/response bodies may contain user-submitted content. If Acme requires strict PII filtering prior to transfer, we will scope redaction work and provide an estimate (redaction is manual/heuristic and may take additional time).

Attachments: proposed-snapshot-steps.txt; forensic-snapshot-manifest.json (template).

I plan to kick off the initial identification query now and will report back with an ETA for the first snapshot (target: within 48 hours).

— Marcus Lin
Sr. Engineering Manager, Site Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Jared Cole <security@acme-corp.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, legal@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-11-22T14:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: RE: Possible customer-impacting incident — request to preserve logs

Thanks Marcus — that approach sounds good. We are concerned primarily about two services: acme-auth and acme-billing (customer ids 9876 and 9910). Export to a US-region encrypted bucket is acceptable; we will provide an S3 ARN and a KMS key ID by EOD.

We also attached a formal legal hold request (PDF) — our legal team asks for a certificate of preservation and a statement that no automatic deletions will occur while the hold is active. Can you confirm those two things? Also, what is the expected ETA for a first downloadable/transferable export?

— Jared
Attachment: legal-hold-request.pdf
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Jared Cole <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, legal@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-11-24T11:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: RE: Possible customer-impacting incident — request to preserve logs

Jared — confirming next steps and commitments: 

- Acknowledgement: Redwood Inference acknowledges receipt of Acme's preservation request and legal-hold PDF. Our legal team will countersign the hold acknowledgement and return it.
- Preservation actions taken: lifecycle deletion has been disabled on the affected indices/buckets scoped to acme-auth and acme-billing for the window 2026-11-21T22:00:00Z through 2026-11-22T02:00:00Z. We have created an immutable forensic snapshot in us-east-1 (snapshot id: FS-20261122-9832).
- Chain-of-custody: we will provide a signed manifest that includes snapshot id, creator, capture timestamp, S3 path, and access log referencing internal accounts (Marcus Lin and Soojin Lee performed capture).
- Export timeline: initial manifest + a downloadable encrypted export (redwood-managed) — target delivery within 48 hours from the snapshot (so by 2026-11-24T11:00:00-05:00). Full push to your S3 bucket (once you provide ARN + KMS) — target within 5 business days.
- Certificate: we will issue a Certificate of Preservation (signed PDF) and confirm that automatic lifecycle deletions are disabled for the scoped objects while the hold is active.

Please confirm whether you also want cross-region copy to eu-west-1. If so, let us know and we will include that in the manifest and provide the estimated timeline for cross-region transfer.

I will follow up with the signed hold document once legal countersigns; Marcus will send the manifest and technical details for retrieval.

— Soojin Lee
Head of Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference
